checks: Simultaneous permutations fixing the selected index preserve positivity and every column balance. The displayed averaged matrix has columns i and j≠i with exactly the stated entries; its c is positive because it is the average of positive off-diagonal entries. The two averaged channel levels give the displayed equation for the sum of other rows.

AM–GM gives the infimum representation of the geometric mean and its unique positive optimizer. Equality under positive averaging is exactly proportionality of all averaged vectors, proved by testing the optimizer of the average in every summand.

Concavity increases the selected row and the sum of the other rows. Substitution of the averaged frontier gives the exact decomposition into two nonnegative terms. Equality requires each of the row averaging gaps to be zero.

For the selected row, coordinate permutations have the same sum and therefore force equal channels. In every other row, permutations fixing that row and the selected column equate the remaining channels; for d=2 that group constraint is vacuous and there is only one such channel. Comparisons across rows align the selected channel and force a common channel ratio.

Each nonselected column balance yields Q_j=B+sum Q_l−1+A, making Q_j independent of j. The selected column then forces P=1/d and the other channel equals (1−A−B)/(d−1). Conversely those channels make the averaging exact without requiring equality of the original nonselected diagonals.

For each x in (0,d), the interval for A is nonempty and enforces B,t,c>0. The actual vertex evaluations have total positive height one, the edge matrix has positive eigenvalues, and the displayed barycentric coefficients are strictly positive and average the vertices to zero. The chosen normals span and sum to zero, all incidences are strict, and the selected row value is x. Exact rational tests for representative interior values in dimensions 2–20 verified the signed evaluations, eigenvalue identities, barycenter, and integer-power frontier identity.

Rescaling each complete ambient inequality by its positive circuit coefficient preserves all halfspaces and multiplies its base and continuous coefficients consistently. The geometry used in the proof applies only to the selected simplex fiber and its strict incidence.
Verified the exact original source digest and §§3–6 locator. The accepted-boundary scope does not include the singular d=1 exponent or traces through a simplex vertex.
